label: D26-hapus-kartu
decision: How should the Anastrophe tracer backend authorize card deletion (FR-31, SDD DELETE /cards/{id}) before user session authentication exists?

candidates.description: DELETE /v1/cards/{card_instance_id} carries a proof of possession for one of the card's credentials: cred_id, a nonce from the existing POST /v1/credentials/{cred}:challenge, and a credential-key signature over "ANP1-REVOKE" ‖ cred_id ‖ nonce ‖ card_instance_id. The server verifies it, revokes the card instance and all its credentials (frees the 8-card slot), and writes credential.revoked audit events. The app signs after the user's confirmation and Face ID/passcode (FR-31 already requires authentication), and stores the server card id at provisioning.
DELETE /v1/cards/{card_instance_id} with no proof: the random card-instance UUID known to the device acts as a capability. The server revokes the card instance and its credentials.

Implement only local deletion in the app now (delete key, record, card); revoke on the server later, once session authentication exists. The server keeps the card instance and credential ACTIVE until certificate expiry and the slot stays used.

priorities: 1) FR-31 must revoke the credential server-side (reader refuses after sync) and free the 8-card slot. 2) A third party must not be able to delete someone else's card. 3) Reuse the accepted renewal pattern (ADR-0023) instead of inventing a new mechanism. 4) Keep it simple and buildable now without session auth. The user approved autonomous iteration; decisions under 0.60 go back to the user.
requirements: The server revokes the card instance and its credentials, freeing the device's card slot.
Deleting a card requires proof that the caller holds the card's credential private key.
No mechanism beyond what the backend and app already have (nonce challenge, credential-key signatures) is needed.
